@blackblarneystone is absolutely right about why someone has to pay for it, but I'm guessing you wonder why people have to pay for their own education. There are a few good reasons.

  1. You're getting the greatest direct benefit, so it's fair for you to bear the cost.
  2. If you're personally invested, you're more likely to apply yourself than if someone else is paying.
  3. Education is expensive and people don't enjoy high taxes because they would either rather spend that money on themselves or work fewer hours to do things they'd rather do than go to work.
  4. As someone with a college education, you're more likely to be relatively high income. Subsidizing your lifestyle is fairly regressive when you consider poor blue color workers toiling away so your comfy desk job isn't burdened by a lot of debt.

There are reasons to have society pay for it via taxation, but these become much less compelling when you move beyond primary and secondary school and apply them to higher education.

  1. Everyone derives benefit from an educated populous due to things like a better economy and less crime.
  2. It opens education to more people who would otherwise be unable to afford it (less of an issue with loans nowadays).
  3. Promising free things to young people is a good way to get them to vote for you ;)
